To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a small number of new patients is referred to the European electrophysiologic community; (ii) a high use of non-invasive diagnostic tests and genetic testing is noted; (iii) EP testing is used mainly in symptomatic patients; and (iv) a high focus on first-degree relative is noted.

the number of new cases of arrhythmogenic syndrons (symptomatic as well as asymptomatic) is rather small, that the clinical work-up consists mainly of noninvasive tests, that the genetic testing is relatively common in patients with LQTS and/or CPVT, that EP testing is commonly used in asymptomatic BS and symptomatic family members, and that most European electrophysiologist focus on first degree relatives when dealing with the family members of an arrhythmogenic syndrome.
the clinical work-up for patients with arrhythmia syndromes is mainly non-invasive and that EP testing in family members is performed in BS and in LQTS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the current clinical practice in the management of patients with suspected arrhythmogenic syndres.
the management of arrhythmogenic syndrons, which is mainly based on non-invasive tests and genetic testing.
the current management strategies in patients with possible arrhythmogenic syndrome and their family members, and the results of this survey will be helpful for future guidelines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the majority of European centres are performing the same diagnostic tests in patients and relatives with suspected arrhythmogenic syndrome and the majority of European EPs would perform an EP study in asymptomatic BS and CPVT patients.
there is a need for a more structured and standardized approach in the management of patients with suspected arrhythmogenic syndrome, especially in asymptomatic family members.
the management of arrhythmogenic syndres in Europe is heterogeneous, and that a more standardised approach is needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no uniform approach to the diagnosis and management of arrhythmogenic syndres.
the majority of European centres have a similar strategy for the management of patients with arrhythmia syndromes.
the management of patients with suspected or proven arrhythmogenic syndres is still mainly non-invasive, but that EP testing is increasingly used, especially for BS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no standard approach in the management of patients with arrhythmia syndromes.
the management of patients with arrhythmia syndromes is heterogeneous, but the majority of centres follow similar management strategies.
the management of patients with arrhythmias of suspected genetic origin is not uniform across Europe, with differences in clinical management, genetic testing and invasive EP testing.
